title: Chickpea and Tomato Curry
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using more hearty ingredients like filling carbs, proteins and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Cook rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a medium saucepan with 500ml (2 cups) water, cover and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins. Fluff the rice with a fork.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, cut the unpeeled pumpkin into 2cm chunks (see Make it yours). Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Start curry: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a large deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the pumpkin, stirring, for 3 mins or until starting to soften. Add the curry paste, masala seasoning, garlic and coriander stems and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant.

Simmer curry: Stir the tomato puree, chickpeas and 250ml (1 cup) water into the pumpkin mixture and bring to the boil. Cover, reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 13 mins or until the pumpkin is tender. Stir in ½ tsp sugar, then remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: While the curry is simmering, coarsely chop the cashews. Divide the rice and chickpea and tomato curry among bowls, then scatter with the cashews and coriander leaves. Enjoy!
Make it yours: Feel free to chop up other veggies you have on hand, such as carrot or capsicum, and add them to the stew for an extra veggie boost.
